jp: 京都[きょうと]の秋[あき]は{とても|av-degree}きれいです。
en: Autumn in Kyoto is very beautiful.
why: とても strengthens an adjective to 'very'; あまり needs a negative.

jp: 先生[せんせい]の話[はなし]は{とても|av-degree}おもしろかったです。
en: The teacher's talk was very interesting.
why: A strongly positive impression of an adjective is とても ('very').

jp: 昨日[きのう]の映画[えいが]を見[み]て、{とても|av-degree}悲[かな]しくなりました。
en: I felt very sad after watching yesterday's movie.
why: A strong feeling is 'very' = とても; あまり would need a negative.

jp: {とても|av-degree}おいしいケーキを、ありがとうございました。
en: Thank you for the very delicious cake.
why: In thanks, とても gives the warm 'very'; あまり cannot open a positive phrase.

jp: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くに、{とても|av-degree}静[しず]かな公園[こうえん]があります。
en: Near the station there is a very quiet park.
why: とても + adjective = 'very'; the others weaken it or need a negative.

jp: この犬[いぬ]は{とても|av-degree}かわいいですね。
en: This dog is very cute, isn't it?
why: とても intensifies the adjective: 'very cute'.

jp: 初[はじ]めて会[あ]った人[ひと]は{とても|av-degree}親切[しんせつ]でした。
en: The person I met for the first time was very kind.
why: とても gives 'very kind'; あまり would make the meaning negative.

jp: 子[こ]どものころ、夏休[なつやす]みが{とても|av-degree}楽[たの]しみでした。
en: As a child, I looked forward to the summer vacation very much.
why: とても marks a strong degree of anticipation.

jp: 空港[くうこう]までは{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}時間[じかん]がかかります。
en: It takes quite a lot of time to get to the airport.
why: かなり states a considerable amount; 少し would mean only a little.

jp: 今日[きょう]の会議[かいぎ]には{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}たくさんの人[ひと]が来[き]ました。
en: Quite a lot of people came to today's meeting.
why: かなり + many = a considerable number; あまり needs a negative.

jp: この町[まち]は十年前[じゅうねんまえ]に比[くら]べて、{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}人[ひと]が増[ふ]えました。
en: Compared with ten years ago, the population of this town has grown considerably.
why: A big measurable increase is かなり (or ずいぶん).

jp: 駅[えき]から{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}遠[とお]いので、タクシーで行[い]きましょう。
en: It's quite far from the station, so let's go by taxi.
why: The taxi suggestion shows the distance is considerable: かなり.

jp: 熱[ねつ]が{かなり/とても/ずいぶん|av-degree}高[たか]いので、今日[きょう]は学校[がっこう]を休[やす]みます。
en: My fever is quite high, so I will stay home from school today.
why: A high fever that justifies staying home needs a strong degree word.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}遅[おそ]くまで勉強[べんきょう]しました。
en: Yesterday I studied until quite late.
why: かなり gives 'quite' for a late hour; あまり and 決して need a negative, and ほとんど cannot modify 遅く.

jp: 二[に]か月[げつ]ダイエットをして、体重[たいじゅう]が{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}減[へ]りました。
en: After two months of dieting, my weight dropped considerably.
why: A clearly noticeable drop is かなり (or ずいぶん).

jp: この辞書[じしょ]は{かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}古[ふる]いですが、まだ使[つか]えます。
en: This dictionary is quite old, but I can still use it.
why: かなり marks a considerable degree of oldness before the contrast with が.

jp: しばらく会[あ]わないうちに、{ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}背[せ]が伸[の]びたね。
en: You've grown a lot taller since I last saw you.
why: ずいぶん expresses surprise at a big change over time.

jp: 久[ひさ]しぶりに来[き]たら、駅[えき]の周[まわ]りが{ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}変[か]わっていた。
en: When I came back after a long time, the area around the station had changed a lot.
why: A surprising amount of change after a long absence is ずいぶん.

jp: {ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}待[ま]たされたよ。もう一時間[いちじかん]だ。
en: I was kept waiting for ages. It's already been an hour.
why: ずいぶん carries the speaker's feeling that it was a long time.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]が{ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}上手[じょうず]になりましたね。
en: Your Japanese has become a lot better, hasn't it?
why: Remarking on striking improvement is ずいぶん.

jp: 夜[よる]なのに、{ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}暑[あつ]いですね。
en: It's night, yet it's awfully hot, isn't it?
why: ずいぶん expresses surprise that the degree exceeds expectation.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]は病気[びょうき]のあと、{ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}元気[げんき]になりました。
en: My grandmother has become a lot healthier since her illness.
why: A marked recovery is ずいぶん; あまり needs a negative.

jp: 三年[さんねん]ぶりの故郷[こきょう]は{ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}静[しず]かになっていた。
en: My hometown, which I saw for the first time in three years, had become a lot quieter.
why: ずいぶん with the result of change over three years.

jp: {ずいぶん/かなり|av-degree}遠[とお]くまで来[き]たね。もう海[うみ]が見[み]えるよ。
en: We've come a long way. You can already see the sea.
why: ずいぶん expresses that the distance covered is more than expected.

jp: 熱[あつ]いので、{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}冷[さ]ましてから飲[の]んでください。
en: It's hot, so please let it cool a little before you drink it.
why: A small amount of time ('a little') is 少し; the others mean 'a lot'.

jp: 今日[きょう]は昨日[きのう]より{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}寒[さむ]いです。
en: Today is a little colder than yesterday.
why: A slight difference in comparison is 少し.

jp: 私[わたし]は英語[えいご]が{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}話[はな]せます。
en: I can speak a little English.
why: 'A little' ability is 少し; とても would claim fluency.

jp: 寝不足[ねぶそく]で、{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}頭[あたま]が痛[いた]いです。
en: I haven't slept enough, so my head hurts a little.
why: A mild symptom is 少し; the others make it a strong one.

jp: 疲[つか]れたので、{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}休[やす]みましょう。
en: I'm tired, so let's rest for a bit.
why: 'For a short while' with 休む is 少し.

jp: 駅[えき]まで{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}歩[ある]きますが、大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]ですか。
en: It's a short walk to the station; is that all right?
why: A short walk, asked about politely, is 少し.

jp: 髪[かみ]を{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}切[き]りました。
en: I had my hair cut a little.
why: A small amount cut is 少し; the others imply a drastic cut.

jp: もう{少[すこ]し/ちょっと|av-degree}ゆっくり話[はな]してください。
en: Please speak a little more slowly.
why: A request for a small adjustment uses もう少し.

jp: {ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}待[ま]って。すぐ戻[もど]るから。
en: Wait a moment. I'll be right back.
why: A casual 'a moment' in a request is ちょっと.

jp: すみません、{ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}教[おし]えてもらえませんか。
en: Excuse me, could you tell me something quickly?
why: ちょっと softens a polite request.

jp: このスープ、{ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}しょっぱいね。
en: This soup is a little salty, isn't it?
why: A mild complaint in casual speech uses ちょっと.

jp: この服[ふく]は私[わたし]には{ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}大[おお]きいです。
en: This outfit is a little big for me.
why: ちょっと means 'slightly' in a gentle remark about size.

jp: 今日[きょう]は{ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}用事[ようじ]があって、早[はや]く帰[かえ]ります。
en: I have a little something to do today, so I'm leaving early.
why: A minor errand is 'a little something': ちょっと.

jp: {ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}窓[まど]を開[あ]けてもいいですか。
en: May I open the window a little?
why: A light, polite request for permission is ちょっと.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]は{ちょっと/少[すこ]し|av-degree}都合[つごう]が悪[わる]いんです。
en: Sunday is a bit inconvenient for me.
why: ちょっと softens a polite refusal to 'a bit inconvenient'.

jp: 最近[さいきん]は{あまり|av-degree}映画[えいが]を見[み]ません。
en: I don't watch movies much these days.
why: あまり + a negative verb = 'not much'.

jp: 朝[あさ]は{あまり|av-degree}食[た]べません。
en: I don't eat much in the morning.
why: あまり + negative means 'not much'; the others cannot go with this negative.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は{あまり|av-degree}勉強[べんきょう]しないので、成績[せいせき]が悪[わる]いです。
en: My younger brother doesn't study much, so his grades are bad.
why: The reason for poor grades is 'not much study': あまり + negative.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は忙[いそが]しくて、{あまり|av-degree}寝[ね]られませんでした。
en: I was busy yesterday and couldn't sleep much.
why: あまり + negative potential = 'not much'.

jp: この本[ほん]はあまり{おもしろくありません|av-degree}。
en: This book isn't very interesting.
why: あまり must be answered by a negative ending.

jp: 今日[きょう]はあまり{寒[さむ]くないです|av-degree}。
en: It isn't very cold today.
why: あまり demands the negative form of the adjective.

jp: 駅[えき]から家[いえ]まであまり{遠[とお]くありません|av-degree}。
en: My house isn't very far from the station.
why: The adjective after あまり is negative.

jp: 昨日[きのう]のテストはあまり{できませんでした|av-degree}。
en: I couldn't do the test very well yesterday.
why: あまり + negative past = 'did not do very well'.

jp: 父[ちち]はあまり{お酒[さけ]を飲[の]みません|av-degree}。
en: My father doesn't drink much alcohol.
d: お酒[さけ]を飲[の]みます
お酒[さけ]を飲[の]みました
お酒[さけ]を飲[の]むでしょう
why: あまり closes with a negative verb.

jp: この辺[へん]はあまり{にぎやかではありません|av-degree}。
en: This area isn't very lively.
why: あまり requires the negative of a na-adjective.
